s: A company has 60 AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. All VPCs in us-east-1 connect to the data center through a shared transit gateway and AWS Direct Connect. Workloads in every VPC must resolve names in the on-premises zone corp.example.com. On-premises servers must resolve records in Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones for aws.example.com. The company does not want to manage DNS servers and wants to minimize the number of resolver endpoints. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: In a shared networking VPC, create only a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Create a forwarding rule for corp.example.com, share it by using AWS RAM, and configure the on-premises DNS servers to forward aws.example.com queries to the outbound endpoint IP addresses.

Deploy two BIND DNS forwarders on Amazon EC2 in a shared VPC, set the DHCP options set in every VPC to use them, and configure them to forward aws.example.com to the Route 53 Resolver and corp.example.com to the on-premises DNS servers.

In a shared networking VPC, create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint and an outbound endpoint. Create a forwarding rule for corp.example.com that targets the on-premises DNS servers through the outbound endpoint, share the rule with the organization by using AWS RAM, and associate it with every VPC. Associate the private hosted zones with the networking VPC, and configure on-premises conditional forwarders for aws.example.com that point to the inbound endpoint IP addresses.
Create Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints in every VPC, and create a forwarding rule for corp.example.com in each account.

w.y: Centralized Route 53 Resolver endpoints in one networking VPC handle both directions: the outbound endpoint plus a forwarding rule shared by AWS RAM serves every VPC, and the inbound endpoint lets on-premises DNS forward aws.example.com queries. This minimizes endpoints and avoids DNS servers, giving the LEAST operational overhead.

o.A: Outbound endpoints only send queries out of AWS; on-premises resolvers need an inbound endpoint to query private hosted zones.
o.B: Works but requires managing, patching and scaling DNS servers, which the company wants to avoid.
o.C: Correct: one pair of endpoints, RAM-shared rule for outbound, inbound endpoint for on-premises queries.
o.D: Meets functionality but multiplies endpoints and rules across 60 accounts, contradicting the requirement to minimize endpoints.

d: LEAST operational overhead; minimize the number of resolver endpoints
